compiler_and_flags: rustc 1.97.0; crate features: sux 0.14.0 default relevant features none, sucds 0.8.3 `intrinsics`; optimisation flags not stated on page (criterion bench profile)
hardware: Apple M5 Max (ARM64, 18 cores, 128 GB), macOS 26.5.2
name: sux-rs
baseline: sucds Rank9Sel and vers-vecs RsVec (Rust crates; also succinctly BitVec), not SDSL directly
workload: rank1 and select1 over 10,000 random positions on identical seeded random bit vectors of 1M and 10M bits at 10/50/90% density, SelectAdapt<Rank9<AddNumBits<BitVec>>>
claimed_speedup: rank1: 9.0-10.8 us per 10,000 queries vs sucds 16.0-17.9 us and vers-vecs 30.0-34.0 us (about 1.6-1.8x vs sucds, 3x vs vers-vecs, derived from page data). select1: 55.8-78.7 us vs sucds 70.8-139.7 us and vers-vecs 174.4-575.6 us (up to about 2.2x vs sucds, up to about 9x vs vers-vecs, derived from page data)
tradeoffs: Space overhead about 32-39% for the rank+select structure benchmarked (vers-vecs is 5-6.5%, far smaller); construction from bits one at a time is 30-120x slower than vers-vecs because there is no bulk-word constructor in the benchmarked version.
caveats: Measured by the rival succinctly project, not the sux authors, on ARM64 only; x86_64 run outstanding. vers-vecs SIMD select path is x86 only so it ran scalar here. Optimisation flags not stated. select1 timings varied up to about 40% run to run, page says read ordering not ratios. Baseline is other Rust crates, not SDSL; the sux-rs README itself only says 'almost always as fast or faster' than other libraries with no numbers (README: https://github.com/vigna/sux-rs). Same author family as the catalogued C++ sux (https://github.com/vigna/sux).

name: sucds
baseline: vers-vecs RsVec and succinctly BitVec (Rust crates), not SDSL
workload: select1 over 10,000 random positions on identical seeded random bit vectors of 1M and 10M bits at 10/50/90% density, Rank9Sel with intrinsics
claimed_speedup: select1: 70.8-139.7 us per 10,000 queries vs vers-vecs 174.4-575.6 us (up to about 6.6x at 1M/90%, roughly 1.3-6.9x across cells, derived from page data) and succinctly 195.9-280 us; rank1 16.0-17.9 us level with succinctly but 1.9x faster than vers-vecs 30.0-34.0 us (derived from page data)
tradeoffs: Rank9Sel space overhead 36% at 1M and 99% at 10M bits vs vers-vecs 5-6.5%; construction one bit at a time, 30-120x slower than vers-vecs.
caveats: Measured by the rival succinctly project on ARM64 only, not by sucds authors; vers-vecs SIMD select ran scalar on ARM64 so its select could improve on x86_64. sux-rs is faster than sucds in the same tables. Select timings noisy (up to about 40%). Optimisation flags not stated. Baseline is not SDSL and vers-vecs is not a widely used incumbent. README has no performance claims.
